item.title: LiMu Emu & Doug: Soccer
item.description: A — directly watched. Directly watched from iSpot's public master and Liberty Mutual's official upload. Doug delivers a motivational speech to his son's youth soccer team before the coach reminds him that parents must remain off the field; LiMu is then revealed among the children. A different child is addressed as Tommy. The coach's use of 'parents' and the companion Playbook's direct address to Doug Jr. establish the family context.

item.title: Parent Teacher Conference (Short)
item.description: D — unresolved. Internet Archive preserves the complete official YouTube watch-page metadata from May 27, 2026, including the 15.061-second runtime, auto-caption and storyboard endpoints, `tiny desk` keyword, and genuine 1280×720 thumbnail. The thumbnail directly matches Tiny Desk's classroom, Doug costume, child-sized chair, background art, and approximately 7.5-second shot, establishing this as a separately delivered Tiny Desk variant despite its Parent Teacher Conference title. Its legal line says 'Based on 2025 survey,' while the recovered 30-second portfolio master says 2024, further proving a versioned delivery. A timestamped May 5 USPTO web-capture exhibit independently preserves a `libertymutual` Reddit promoted-video card using the exact official short description and a thumbnail of Doug seated in the same classroom/tiny-chair setup, proving paid-social distribution no later than that date. The exhibit does not expose an ad ID or moving asset. The signed YouTube MP4, caption, and storyboard URLs have expired and were not archived, so dialogue, other visible characters, and exact 15-second assembly remain unresolved. Only Doug is retained as a verified appearance edge.

item.title: Tiny Desk
item.description: A — directly watched. Recovered from the authorized Vimeo embed in David Hoffman's portfolio and directly inspected without audible playback; its auto-caption track was checked against local transcription. Doug and his wife meet Doug Jr.'s teacher in an elementary classroom. LiMu appears in the opening title shot; Doug Jr. is discussed but not shown. Doug spends roughly twelve seconds forcing himself into a child-sized chair before asking how his son is doing. Vimeo's April 11 creator-upload date postdates Liberty Mutual's February 20 official upload and is not treated as the premiere. This directly verifies a premise distinct from the misspelled-paper/mustache Parent Teacher Conference reel. The April 24 Parent Teacher Conference (Short) description centers on the same undersized-chair gag and is probably a short cut of Tiny Desk, but edit identity remains unresolved until that footage is recovered.

item.title: S Is For
item.description: D — unresolved. A surviving search-engine record preserves Liberty Mutual's verified official upload, exact title, February 20, 2026 publication date, and description: 'Any moment can be a teachable moment when it comes to Doug and saving money with Liberty Mutual.'

item.title: Math
item.description: D — unresolved. A surviving search-engine record preserves Liberty Mutual's verified official upload, exact title, February 20, 2026 publication date, and description: 'The curriculum has slightly changed since Doug was in school. But Liberty Mutual customizing car insurance so you only pay for what you need, has not.'

item.title: Love
item.description: A — directly watched. Directly watched from Liberty Mutual's official upload. The pair extend their romantic/shared-idiolect mini-campaign with an increasingly recursive declaration of love and savings. Agent Opus's frozen April 30 Meta snapshot also contains two distinct 15-second paid-social assets using love-and-savings copy. Asset 936496825506296 says, `Do you love how much we love how much you love saving money? We do too`; asset 1427251682142336 says, `Savings is our love language.` The first closely echoes this reel's recursive construction, but expired media prevents a visual or soundtrack match, so neither asset is assigned as this master or a variant.

item.title: Swoon
item.description: A — directly watched. Directly watched from Liberty Mutual's official upload and checked against its caption track. The romantic follow-up turns Marsha's verb 'swoon' into the Struggling Actor's mistaken plural bird noun 'swoons'; no birds actually appear in the reel. Little Black Book's embedded 15-second production master was independently recovered and silently frame-matched to this edit.

item.title: Swoon (Short)
item.description: A — directly watched. Directly watched from Liberty Mutual's official upload. This material variant substitutes a swans/birds misunderstanding for the full Swoon's swoon/majestic-birds exchange; no birds appear.

item.title: LiMu Emu & Doug: Parent Teacher Conference
item.description: A — directly watched. Recovered through iSpot's March 14, 2026 Internet Archive snapshot, whose Open Graph metadata exposed the still-live public CDN master. The complete 30-second MP4 was downloaded and directly inspected without audible playback; its classroom action, speakers, title shot, paper text, and timing align with the independently preserved GDELT broadcast transcript. Doug and a woman presented as his wife attend a meeting with Doug Jr.'s teacher; the child appears behind them dressed as a miniature Doug, complete with mustache and uniform, and silently displays 'Insurense is dumb.' LiMu appears only in the opening title shot. Liberty Mutual's later private upload supplies an April 24 posting date, while iSpot supplies the earlier February 4 catalog date. The separate official `Mustache` upload remains an alias/possible alternate edit because its footage has not been recovered.

item.title: Dating App (Short)
item.description: A — directly watched. Directly watched from Liberty Mutual's current official upload. This is a material alternate exchange from the same waterfront date, not merely a truncation of Dating App. Internet Archive preserves a now-private earlier official upload, d6Pz0Evx7OQ: its watch page identifies the same official title, a 15-second runtime, January 16 publication, matching description, and auto-caption track; its genuine thumbnail shows the same pair and set. The older upload establishes the corrected release date, although its expired media/storyboard URLs prevent a binary or shot-for-shot identity claim with the current April 24 upload.

item.title: Truth Tellers: Dating App
item.description: A — directly watched. Directly watched from Liberty Mutual's official upload and checked against its caption track. The Struggling Actor meets Marsha through an 'inter-web' dating app; she mirrors his idiolect, including 'phone-puter,' 'bondling,' 'Biberty,' 'la-zag-na,' and 'can-ooo-lis.' Their opening 'I am' exchange is audibly stylized but not respelled beyond the official captions. A stylized heart appears as they spin together. Little Black Book's embedded 30-second production master was independently recovered and silently frame-matched to this edit. Its production account calls this the first mini-campaign in a new season and says the wave was shot over two days in Los Angeles in mid-December 2025; Dating App went from shoot to shipment in eight days. Lindsay Foster's identification is corroborated by contemporaneous commercial coverage and her own reported social post, not by the reel credits.

item.title: Say the Word on Beat: LiMu Emu & Doug Edition
item.description: A — directly watched. Directly watched from Liberty Mutual's official Shorts feed. This is a non-narrative timing game built from still images: Doug/mug (easy), Doug/mug/outlet (medium), Doug/mug/outlet/pug (hard), and LiMu/another emu (expert). Retained as an official social reel but not treated as an in-story event.

item.title: Coin Flip
item.description: A — directly watched. Directly watched from Liberty Mutual's official upload. A press-conference parody featuring a customized LiMu coin and two oversized mascot-like Doug and LiMu figures; promotional sports integration, not evidence of another fictional continuity.

Doug and LiMu skydive toward a football stadium but land in its parking lot; their parachutes then drag them across the pavement until LiMu bites through the lines, after which they continue on foot.

The human-character recurrence is explicit; no individual bird identity is established.

item.title: Streaker (Short)
item.description: A — directly watched. Directly watched from Liberty Mutual's official upload. Unlike the 30-second master, this edit has LiMu on the field and Doug tackled by security, with no pants/censor-bar joke.

item.title: College Cuber
item.description: A — directly watched. Directly inspected from Dylan Sadiq's original paid-partnership TikTok, recovered through Gondola's exact post record. The 47.553-second vertical reel carries persistent `#ad` disclosure and the caption `Day 59 of never finishing my artwork 😭 Glad I got LiMu Emu to stay still long enough for this one @Liberty Mutual #paidpartnership`. Sadiq repeatedly assembles, disrupts, and rebuilds a framed Rubik's-cube mosaic before revealing LiMu and Doug beneath a Liberty logo panel. LiMu and Doug appear only as mosaic subjects, not performed characters in the scene; the character edges are retained for depiction indexing. Local automatic transcription returned the same possible sung phrase twice with poor log probability and high no-speech probability, so no lyric is asserted. Independent 2026 LIT and MUSE entrant records provide the later award title, official stills, and partial production credits. Retained as creator branded content, not an in-story event.

item.title: LiMu Emu & Doug: Streaker
item.description: A — directly watched. Directly watched from iSpot's public master. Doug runs onto a football field after mistaking the opposing team's bird mascot for LiMu, loses his trousers during the pursuit, and is covered by an on-screen censor bar; LiMu remains at the sideline.

item.title: Truth Tellers: Biberty Baby
item.description: A — directly watched. Directly watched from iSpot's public master. The Struggling Actor sits beside Liberty Mom and Baby, repeatedly corrects the baby's pronunciation to his own 'Biberty' flub, then argues with the two-year-old. The on-screen offer states that Mom saved $950 by bundling home and auto insurance. This directly combines the Bad Job and First Word character branches.

item.title: LiMu Emu and Doug: Farmer
item.description: A — directly watched. Directly watched from iSpot's public master. An emu wearing LiMu's later uniform leaves a farm while Frank predicts failure and a woman calls the bird a dreamer; five years later Frank sees LiMu and Doug on television. The reel explicitly presents this origin-story frame, but does not name the woman or establish further biography. Official-channel release appears to be January 2, 2025, after iSpot's December 30 catalog date.

item.title: Doug Gets LiMu-ified
item.description: A — directly watched. Directly watched from Liberty Mutual's official silent download and verified against its caption track. David Hoffman begins as Doug while makeup artist Jo Steel, herself costumed as Doug, applies a practical beak, face treatment, and feathers to turn him into a human LiMu imitation.

item.title: Halloween Magic With a Whole Lotta Feathers
item.description: A — directly watched. Directly watched from Jo Steel's silent creator upload and verified against its caption track. This compact companion reveals Steel's feathered human-LiMu makeup beside Hoffman as Doug.

item.description: A — directly watched. Directly watched from Jo Steel's silent creator upload and verified against its caption track. Steel starts dressed as Doug and time-lapses her own practical transformation into a human LiMu imitation; David Hoffman appears as Doug for the final duo pose.

item.title: LiMu Emu and Doug: Weird Dream
item.description: A — directly watched. Directly watched from iSpot's public master. Giant parade-balloon versions of Doug and LiMu collide with street furniture and deflate; the scene is revealed as a nightly recurring dream Doug is recounting to a therapist, with LiMu present in the therapy room.

item.title: Truth Tellers: Wax
item.description: A — directly watched. Directly watched from iSpot's public master and checked against the official-video/secondary transcript trail. The speaker's life-size wax double melts in the boardwalk heat just as he says it will stand the test of time.

item.title: Stilts
item.description: A — directly watched. No editorial note has been added.

item.title: LiMu Emu and Doug: Firepole
item.description: A — directly watched. Directly watched from iSpot's public master. Doug slides down an office firepole expecting LiMu to follow, but LiMu takes the elevator and is already waiting in the parking garage. Stacie Greenwell appears behind the same supervisor-style desk and is addressed as Chief; shared performer, workplace, and authority role make recurrence plausible, but no personal name or explicit memory links this Chief to Helicopter's supervisor.

item.title: LiMu Emu and Doug: Ghostbusters Frozen Empire
item.description: A — directly watched. Directly watched from iSpot's public master. Mini-Pufts overrun the yellow car while Doug phones the Ghostbusters and is placed on hold. The film title card makes this an explicit Ghostbusters: Frozen Empire co-promotion, retained with the promotional-crossover asterisk. Tie-in chronology reports first TV airing March 8 and official posting March 11; iSpot catalogs March 22.

item.title: Again
item.description: A — directly watched. Directly watched from a surviving public copy after the official upload became private. This is a 15-second companion reel, correcting the provisional 30-second runtime. The baby repeatedly asks for the mother's savings story and supplies the last Liberty in the jingle; the official description says the story has been requested 3,456 times.

item.title: Truth Tellers: First Word
item.description: A — directly watched. Directly watched from iSpot's public master. The mother's repeated savings pitch has displaced expected family words: the baby's first spoken word is Liberty, repeated for Mama, Auntie, and the final beat of the jingle. Official YouTube publication followed on January 2. An agency award entry confirms the mother, her sister, and the mother's firstborn relationship structure.

item.title: Emu and Doug: Replaced
item.description: A — directly watched. Directly watched from iSpot's public master. The same performer and Biberty malapropism from Bad Job enter the LiMu/Doug production layer: a director reads a plan to crush Doug with a piano, identifies the Struggling Actor as his replacement, and the actor answers Doug's mustache objection by applying a false one. This is a direct on-screen bridge between the two campaign branches.

item.title: Dog Walker
item.description: A — directly watched. Directly watched from iSpot's public master. The speaker says her savings funded a dog-walking business; five of the six dogs chase a rabbit while the Great Dane remains seated. The spoken dog names are transcribed as Taco, Sesame, Walter, Archie, and Duchess; none is treated as a recurring character without another appearance.

item.title: The Reminder
item.description: A — directly watched. Directly watched from iSpot's public master. A mother warns her adult daughter about shopping, learns about the advertised savings, and discovers a forgotten paper reminder to collect the daughter's father from the airport.

item.title: Like Father, Like Son
item.description: A — directly watched. Directly watched from iSpot's public master. Doug explicitly calls the boy his son and sends him out in a miniature yellow car with a juvenile emu. The boy calls LiMu “Uncle LiMu”; this establishes the form of address but does not by itself settle whether the relationship is literal or honorary. The juvenile emu's Lil LiMu label remains catalog/secondary metadata because it is not spoken in the cut.

item.title: Electric Unicycle
item.description: A — directly watched. Directly watched from iSpot's public master. A couple spend their advertised $652 savings on electric unicycles; the man rides off the pier, and the woman casually advises him to doggie-paddle. The iSpot record is dated December 31, 2022 even though secondary coverage and viewer discussion cluster in early 2023, so the catalog date governs the chronology unless earlier provenance emerges.

item.title: LiMu Emu and Doug: Car Wash
item.description: A — directly watched. Directly watched from iSpot's public master, visually confirming David Hoffman as Doug despite his omission from the catalog cast field. Doug pitches safe-driver savings to a man moving slowly through a car wash; the man emerges exhilarated and asks to go again.

item.title: Bowling
item.description: A — directly watched. Directly watched from iSpot's public master. Doug celebrates his own bowling, then encourages LiMu to roll a ball; LiMu's result is immediately disqualified from their scorekeeping.

item.title: Pie Eating Contest
item.description: A — directly watched. Directly watched from iSpot's public master. The announcer delivers the full sponsorship message before starting the contest, at which point a flock of seagulls descends on the pies. Any identity link to the Great Day bird or later Struggling Actor bird remains an unverified hypothesis.

item.title: Heartwarming
item.description: A — directly watched. Directly watched from iSpot's public master. A mother gives her daughter a wedding veil while a narrator repeatedly interrupts the emotional exchange with the home-insurance message. iSpot catalogs the surviving page on 2023-04-01, but contemporaneous production coverage establishes the reel in the July 2022 campaign wave.

item.title: Catchy Song

item.title: Romance
item.description: A — directly watched. Directly watched from the public 30-second Vimeo master. A couple enact a rain-soaked romantic confession inside their flooded house; the insurance pitch interrupts and redirects the expected declaration of love.

A Liberty Mutual representative introduces a miniature house and a pool-party mnemonic; a guest arrives carrying a yellow insurance box before another guest backflips into the pool. Also described as Young People in trade coverage; iSpot's Pool Party title is used for the reel record.

item.title: LiMu Emu and Doug: Tools
item.description: A — directly watched. Directly watched from iSpot's public master. While Doug works under the Liberty van, LiMu repeatedly supplies the wrong objects but correctly brings the phone needed for the sales pitch; the repair attempt ends with Doug requesting a mechanic.

item.title: Fishing: Minions: The Rise of Gru
item.description: A — directly watched. Directly watched from iSpot's public master. A fisherman on the waterfront hooks a Minion-like yellow submarine that surfaces beside him before the explicit Minions: The Rise of Gru theatrical tag. Retain as an asterisked co-marketing reel, not automatic evidence of core shared continuity.

item.title: Emu Wedding
item.description: A — directly watched. Directly watched from iSpot's public master. Doug officiates LiMu's wedding to Linda; another emu objects and Doug addresses him as Kevin. Relationship between Linda and the female emu previously called LiMu's wife remains unresolved; Linda's name is not audible in this cut and still depends on secondary identification.

item.title: Knitting
item.description: A — directly watched. Directly watched from iSpot's public master. Two knitters on the waterfront competitively reveal a scarf, a backpack, a tuxedo, and matching booties made for Marco, the seated dog between them.

item.title: Radar Speed Gun
item.description: A — directly watched. Directly watched from iSpot's public master. Doug clocks LiMu running past the parked Liberty car at 34 miles per hour; LiMu continues out of sight rather than stopping for the assignment.

item.title: Bird Call
item.description: A — directly watched. Directly watched from iSpot's public master. Doug uses a bird-call whistle after LiMu fails to answer; chickens, swans, penguins, pigeons, and other birds gather before LiMu finally returns carrying a flying disc.

item.title: Chocolate Letters / Treats
item.description: D — unresolved. Copper Giants' award entry and its February 24, 2026 LBB production report both describe another shorter reel in the Dating App mini-campaign involving a box of treats and a message whose letters taste like chocolate. February 24 is retained as a latest-attested existence bound, not assumed to be its public release date. The formerly mysterious private Truth Tellers playlist slot d6Pz0Evx7OQ is now excluded: its archived official watch page identifies it as an earlier upload of Dating App (Short). The award entry's five hidden full-resolution gallery images have now been recovered and inspected; all depict the watched 30-second Dating App reel and none shows treats or chocolate letters. A fresh inventory of the live official Truth Tellers playlist exposed nine public IDs, all already mapped to watched canon records, and no treats candidate. Agent Opus's April 30 Meta-ad snapshot contains several six- and ten-second assets promoted with `sweet tooth` and `make your day sweeter` copy. That language makes the paid-social group a plausible recovery lead for this scenario, but expired media and thumbnails prevent identification; no asset is assigned to this reel. Title, runtime, dialogue, release date, and original distribution surface remain unresolved.
